main_text.l: Nos,fratres carisimi,patientes simus, & stabiliamus corda nostra: quoniā adventus Domini appropinquat. Ne ingemiscamus alij adversus alios, ut ne condemnemur: ecce, Judex ante januam astat: Jac.5.9. Bonam autem caussam bene agamus: nec Antagonistarum more, conviciis odijsque certemus: nec abeo quod malum est,nos vinci patiamur: sed vincamus bonitate maliciam: Rom.12. versu ultimo.

l.i: Ecce extollit se is, cuius anima non est recta in eo: Justus autem fide sua vivet.

main_text.l: Sicut uniones & gemmæ,non magnitudine, sed precio,elegantia & aliis modis, saxa longè vincunt: ita hoc aureum dictum,mira brevitate res summas complectitur. Deus det nobis, ut illud pie ὀρθοτομίαν posimus.

Propositio orationis Jehovæ, tradita in hoc versu 4, constat ἀντίθεσις Injusti & Justi: quorum ille sese extollere,id est,brevi tempore supra alios sese efferre, eminere & florere: hic autem fide sua in æ-ternum vivere,dicitur.

page.notes: Printed "Ecce" carries a stroke over the e, not transcribed. The Greek word ἀντίθεσις and the Greek word ὀρθοτομίαν are read from a small scan and are doubtful: [?] was not added because the forms are the expected ones, but they should be checked. The left-margin note has no reference mark in the text. Printed "fe is" and "fide fua" use long s, transcribed as plain s. Verse number "4," and references Jac.5.9 and Rom.12. are copied as printed. Line "Quia" at foot treated as catchword.
